## ✨ New Features

### Configure public schema factories with reusable object defaults ([#28604](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28604))

[`SchemaFactory`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class) now accepts an options object with the scope and an [`objectOptions`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactoryoptions-interface#objectoptions-propertysignature) property bag through the public API. The property bag provides reusable defaults for [`object`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#object-method) and [`objectRecursive`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#objectrecursive-method), including the public `allowUnknownOptionalFields` option. Options passed directly to an object schema override factory defaults through a shallow merge.

```typescript
import { SchemaFactory } from "fluid-framework";

const sf = new SchemaFactory({
  scope: "com.example",
  objectOptions: {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: true,
  },
});

class Person extends sf.object("Person", { name: sf.string }) {}

// Override the default for one schema.
class StrictPerson extends sf.object(
  "StrictPerson",
  { name: sf.string },
  { allowUnknownOptionalFields: false },
) {}
```

You can read and extend factory settings without changing the original factory:

- [`settings`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#settings-property) provides the factory's options without its scope.
- [`scopedFactory`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#scopedfactory-method) creates a child factory by merging provided object-option properties with the current settings, without changing the original factory.

```typescript
const extended = sf.scopedFactory("strict", {
  objectOptions: {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: false,
  },
});
```

Passing `{}` or `{ objectOptions: {} }` preserves inherited settings. Metadata and persisted metadata, when supported, are replaced as whole objects when provided; they are not deep-merged. To start without inherited settings, construct a new factory with the desired scope.

The beta and alpha schema factories support their corresponding tier-specific options.

## 🌳 SharedTree DDS Changes

### Add an alpha API to check if a node has content in unknown optional fields ([#28529](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28529))

Object nodes whose schema sets [allowUnknownOptionalFields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) can contain optional fields that are not in the view schema. The content of these fields is not available through the node's properties.

The new `TreeAlpha.hasUnknownChildren` API returns `true` if a node has content in at least one unknown optional field. To read that content, use `TreeAlpha.exportVerbose` with `KeyEncodingOptions.allStoredKeys`.

```typescript
const sf = new SchemaFactoryBeta("com.example");
class Person extends sf.object(
  "Person",
  { name: sf.string },
  { allowUnknownOptionalFields: true },
) {}

// ...

// A newer version of the application added a `nickname` field.
if (TreeAlpha.hasUnknownChildren(person)) {
  const content = TreeAlpha.exportVerbose(person, {
    keys: KeyEncodingOptions.allStoredKeys,
  });
  // { type: "com.example.Person", fields: { name: "Alice", nickname: "Ali" } }
}
```

### Reduce navigation overhead for SharedTree reads and edits ([#28554](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28554))

SharedTree reads, edits, and parent/key queries have lower overhead, including in deeply nested trees. No application code or stored document format changes are required.

#### Performance measurements

Benchmarks on trees nested ten levels deep measure improvements with both the [reference (default) forest](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/#foresttypereference-variable) and the [optimized forest](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/#foresttypeoptimized-variable). Times are microseconds per benchmark iteration.

| Forest | Workload | Before | After | Less elapsed time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference (default) | Object and array reads | 5.349 | 1.626 | 69.6% |
| Reference (default) | Edits | 138.518 | 115.525 | 16.6% |
| Reference (default) | Parent/key queries | 13.577 | 0.728 | 94.6% |
| Optimized | Object and array reads | 3.610 | 1.593 | 55.9% |
| Optimized | Edits | 112.610 | 97.693 | 13.2% |
| Optimized | Parent/key queries | 7.011 | 0.635 | 90.9% |

Results are means from two fresh processes per version, run serially in balanced order on Linux x64 with Node.js 22.22.3 and production emulation enabled. These are workload-specific results on a shared host, not whole-application speedups. Edit measurements are noisier, with relative margins of error up to approximately 20%, so treat those differences with caution.

### Remove deprecated TreeBranch and TreeBranchAlpha type aliases ([#28284](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28284))

The deprecated `TreeBranch` and `TreeBranchAlpha` compatibility aliases have been removed. Use [`UntypedTreeView`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/untypedtreeview-interface) and [`UntypedTreeViewAlpha`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/untypedtreeviewalpha-interface) instead.

```typescript
// Before
import type { TreeBranch } from "fluid-framework/beta";
import type { TreeBranchAlpha } from "fluid-framework/alpha";

// After

import type { UntypedTreeViewAlpha } from "fluid-framework/alpha";
```

### Preserve array and map node types when accessing alpha APIs ([#28579](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28579))

Calling [`asAlpha`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework#asalpha-function) on an array or map node now preserves its read and insertion types, customized subclass members, and schema identity. The additional alpha methods use the node's existing read and insertion types, so valid content remains accepted and invalid content remains rejected.

Omit the type arguments to preserve the complete node type automatically. If you already specify the allowed types explicitly, that call remains supported, but it does not preserve customized members in the returned type. Specify the node type as the second type argument to preserve those members too.

```typescript
import { asAlpha, SchemaFactory } from "fluid-framework/alpha";

const sf = new SchemaFactory("example");
class Numbers extends sf.array("Numbers", sf.number) {
  public label = "numbers";
}
const numbers = new Numbers([1, 2]);

// Recommended: infer the element type and preserve the custom label property.
const inferred = asAlpha(numbers);
inferred.unshift(0);
inferred.label; // string

// An explicit allowed-types argument still supports numeric array operations.
const explicit = asAlpha<typeof sf.number>(numbers);
explicit.unshift(3);

// Also specify the node type to preserve the custom label property.
const explicitNode = asAlpha<typeof sf.number, Numbers>(numbers);
explicitNode.label; // string
```

The same type-argument guidance applies to map nodes. The conversion still returns the original node without changing runtime behavior.

### Track annotations across array and formatted text edits ([#27621](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/27621))

You can now track ranges with application-defined data, such as review comments, through edits to arrays and formatted text. The new alpha APIs `ExtrinsicLocations.createArraySchema` and `FormattedText.createSchemaWithRanges` provide this capability. Both expose ranges and their associated data through a `ranges` property.

These APIs are early `@alpha` features and are not yet production-ready. Configure SharedTree with `minVersionForCollab` of at least `2.80.0`. In this early `@alpha` version, concurrent changes anywhere in the document can reject a content or range edit rather than merge it: this version is intended for API experimentation and feedback, not production use.

#### Arrays

Use [`ExtrinsicLocations`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/extrinsiclocations-namespace) to create an array schema with tracked ranges. Edit content through `transactOnContent` to maintain ranges across insertions, removals, and moves. You can use synchronous nested `runTransaction` calls inside its callback. If a nested transaction rolls back content edits, the range endpoints are restored before that transaction call returns.

```typescript
import {
  ExtrinsicLocations,
  SchemaFactoryBeta,
} from "@fluidframework/tree/alpha";

const sf = new SchemaFactoryBeta("com.example.review");
class Document extends ExtrinsicLocations.createArraySchema({
  schemaFactory: sf,
  rangeDataSchema: sf.string,
  contentSchema: sf.string,
}) {}

const document = Document.create(["Plan", "Build", "Ship"]);
const comment = document.ranges.trackRange(
  "comment",
  { start: 1, end: 3 },
  "Check these steps",
);
document.transactOnContent((content) => content.insertAt(0, "Design"));
document.content.slice(comment.start.index, comment.end.index); // ["Build", "Ship"]
```

#### Formatted text

Use [`FormattedText.createSchemaWithRanges`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/formattedtext-namespace) for text whose existing editing methods maintain ranges automatically. It accepts named options for the schema factory, formatting, additional atom schemas, default formatting, and range data schema.

Formatted text implementations now reserve the `ranges` property name, including schemas created with the existing `FormattedText.createSchema` Alpha API. If your subclass defines this property, rename it to avoid a collision with the implementation. Assignments to this property can now throw a `TypeError`, even though the existing factory's return type does not prevent the collision.

```typescript
import {
  FormattedText,
  SchemaFactoryBeta,
  TreeViewConfiguration,
  createIndependentTreeAlpha,
} from "@fluidframework/tree/alpha";

const sf = new SchemaFactoryBeta("com.example.annotatedText");
class Format extends sf.object("Format", { bold: sf.boolean }) {}
class Comment extends sf.object("Comment", { message: sf.string }) {}
class Text extends FormattedText.createSchemaWithRanges({
  schemaFactory: sf,
  formatSchema: Format,
  extraAtoms: [],
  defaultFormatInsertable: { bold: false },
  rangeDataSchema: Comment,
}) {}

const view = createIndependentTreeAlpha({
  minVersionForCollab: "2.80.0",
}).viewWith(new TreeViewConfiguration({ schema: Text }));
view.initialize(Text.fromString("Hello world"));
const text = view.root;
const comment = text.ranges.trackRange(
  "comment",
  { start: 6, end: 11 },
  { message: "Review this word" },
);
text.insertAt(0, "Say: ");
const { start, end } = comment; // start.index === 11, end.index === 16
text.getString(start.index, end.index); // "world"
```

Existing formatted text can be upgraded to support ranges without rewriting its content. See the `FormattedText` namespace documentation for details.

### Fix nodeChanged events for changes to unknown optional fields ([#28577](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28577))

When another client changed an [unknown optional field](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) of an object node, subscribing to `nodeChanged` on that node caused an error to be thrown when the change was applied. This also affected `TreeAlpha.trackObservations`, `TreeAlpha.trackObservationsOnce`, and React components using observation tracking from `@fluidframework/react`, such as `useTreeObservations` and `withTreeObservations`.

Now `nodeChanged` is emitted for these changes. Unknown optional fields have no property, so they are not included in `changedProperties`. Instead, the new `changedUnknownProperties` property of the event data lists their stored keys. If only unknown optional fields changed, `changedProperties` is empty.

```typescript
TreeBeta.on(
  node,
  "nodeChanged",
  ({ changedProperties, changedUnknownProperties }) => {
    // changedProperties: property keys of known fields that changed.
    // changedUnknownProperties: stored keys of unknown optional fields that changed, or undefined if none changed.
  },
);
```

Observation tracking is invalidated when an unknown optional field changes if the tracked code observed it, for example by calling `TreeAlpha.hasUnknownChildren`.

### Applications can configure the policy for tolerating unknown optional fields through the public API ([#28603](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28603))

[`SchemaFactory.object`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/schemafactory-class#object-method) and [`SchemaFactory.objectRecursive`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/schemafactory-class#objectrecursive-method) now accept the [`allowUnknownOptionalFields`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) option through the public API. The option defaults to `true`.

This option controls how an object node's view schema handles optional fields that are declared in the document's stored schema but not in the view schema:

- Set `allowUnknownOptionalFields` to `true` to let an older application version continue to view and edit a document after a newer version adds new optional fields to the object schema, provided the schemas are otherwise compatible. The older version cannot access those fields through its view. Copying nodes by reading their fields or spreading them into new nodes can drop data in the unknown fields.
- Set `allowUnknownOptionalFields` to `false` to prevent viewing documents whose stored schema declares additional optional fields for that object. After a newer application version adds an optional field to the object schema, older versions with this policy cannot view the document until their view schemas include that field.

```typescript
import { SchemaFactory } from "@fluidframework/tree";

const factory = new SchemaFactory("com.example");

class Person extends factory.object(
  "Person",
  { name: factory.string },
  // Reject documents with additional optional fields on Person.
  { allowUnknownOptionalFields: false },
) {}
```

The beta `ObjectSchemaOptions` type is renamed to `ObjectSchemaOptionsBeta`. If you reference the beta type directly, update those references to the new name.

### Add an alpha API to get the schema of unknown fields ([#28563](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28563))

The new `TreeContextAlpha.unknownFieldSchemas` property maps each object node schema that has [unknown fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) to the schema of those fields, keyed by stored key. The value updates when the document's stored schema changes: listen to the view's [`schemaChanged`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treeviewevents-interface#schemachanged-methodsignature) event to know when to read it again. It is available on [`TreeViewAlpha`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treeviewalpha-interface) and on the [context](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#context-methodsignature) of any hydrated node. It is `undefined` for [unhydrated](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/unhydrated-typealias) nodes, which have no view schema.

To read the content of these fields, use [`TreeAlpha.exportVerbose`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#exportverbose-methodsignature) with [`KeyEncodingOptions.allStoredKeys`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/keyencodingoptions-enum#allstoredkeys-enummember).

#### Example

Version 1 of an application defines a `Person` with a `name` field, and allows unknown optional fields. [`allowUnknownOptionalFields`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) will be enabled by default in the 3.10 release.

```typescript
const sf = new SchemaFactoryBeta("com.example");
class Person extends sf.object(
  "Person",
  { name: sf.string },
  { allowUnknownOptionalFields: true },
) {}
```

Version 2 of the application adds an optional `nickname` field:

```typescript
class Person extends sf.object(
  "Person",
  { name: sf.string, nickname: sf.optional(sf.string) },
  { allowUnknownOptionalFields: true },
) {}
```

Version 1 can still open a document after version 2 upgrades its schema, but the `nickname` field is unknown to it. Version 1 can use `unknownFieldSchemas` to find the schema of that field, then use `exportVerbose` to read its content:

```typescript
// In version 1 of the application:
const fieldSchemas = TreeAlpha.context(person).unknownFieldSchemas?.get(Person);
// Map { "nickname" => { kind: FieldKind.Optional, simpleAllowedTypes: Map { "com.fluidframework.leaf.string" => ... }, ... } }

const content = TreeAlpha.exportVerbose(person, {
  keys: KeyEncodingOptions.allStoredKeys,
});
// { type: "com.example.Person", fields: { name: "Ali", nickname: "Al" } }
```

### Object schemas support unknown optional fields by default ([#28606](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28606))

Object schemas created by [`SchemaFactory`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class), [`SchemaFactoryBeta`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactorybeta-class), and [`SchemaFactoryAlpha`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactoryalpha-class) now allow unknown optional fields by default universally. This makes older application versions forward-compatible with documents whose stored schema has added optional fields, without requiring every object schema to specify `allowUnknownOptionalFields: true`.

Applications that require an exact match between the object view schema and stored schema can retain the previous behavior by explicitly setting `allowUnknownOptionalFields: false`. The `allowUnknownOptionalFields` option is available on the public [`SchemaFactory.object`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#object-methodsignature) API:

```typescript
const schemaFactory = new SchemaFactory("com.example");

class StrictPerson extends schemaFactory.object(
  "Person",
  {
    name: schemaFactory.string,
  },
  {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: false,
  },
) {}
```

Applications can also set `allowUnknownOptionalFields: false` once on the public [`SchemaFactory`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class) to preserve the previous default for all object schemas created by that factory. Set the factory's [`objectOptions`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactoryoptions-interface#objectoptions-propertysignature) property bag when constructing it:

```typescript
const factory = new SchemaFactory({
  scope: "com.example",
  objectOptions: {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: false,
  },
});
```

Individual schemas can still override this factory default.

#### Behavior to review

Code that reads only known properties does not observe unknown fields. As a result, application implementations of cloning, equality, serialization, or object reconstruction may omit unknown data even though SharedTree preserves it internally. Spreading a node into a new object also includes only the known view-schema properties. Review any code that round-trips a node by reading its known properties and constructing a replacement, since such code may silently discard unknown fields.

For example, an older client may define `Person` with only a `name` field:

```typescript
class Person extends schemaFactory.object("Person", {
  name: schemaFactory.string,
}) {}
```

After a newer client adds an optional `nickname` field, the older client can still read the document, but this custom clone loses the unknown field:

```typescript
function clonePerson(person: Person): Person {
  return new Person({ name: person.name });
}
```

Calling `clonePerson` omits `nickname` because the older view does not expose that property, even though SharedTree preserved it on the original node.

Use [`TreeBeta.clone`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treebeta-interface#clone-methodsignature) to clone a hydrated tree, which will preserve unknown fields and the source document's schema context. When exporting, [`TreeAlpha.exportVerbose`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#exportverbose-methodsignature) preserves unknown fields only when configured to use all stored keys.

```typescript
const exported = TreeAlpha.exportVerbose(person, {
  keys: KeyEncodingOptions.allStoredKeys,
});
```

Using `KeyEncodingOptions.knownStoredKeys` or `KeyEncodingOptions.usePropertyKeys` omits unknown optional fields. Unhydrated nodes created using constructors or insertable content have no source document schema from which unknown fields could be interpreted. [`TreeAlpha.importVerbose`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#importverbose-methodsignature) currently rejects unexpected fields, including when the target schema allows unknown optional fields. Support for preserving these fields through import and export should be added in follow-up work.

Applications whose code depends on enumerating every field, reconstructs nodes from their known properties, or requires schema equality rather than forward compatibility should set `allowUnknownOptionalFields: false` on the affected object schemas:

```typescript
class StrictPerson extends schemaFactory.object(
  "Person",
  {
    name: schemaFactory.string,
  },
  {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: false,
  },
) {}
```

#### Schema compatibility snapshots

Applications using [`snapshotSchemaCompatibility`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/alpha/snapshotschemacompatibility-function) with object schemas from any schema factory will see snapshot-test failures because the serialized view schema changes from `allowUnknownOptionalFields: false` to `allowUnknownOptionalFields: true`. Review the affected schemas, retain historical snapshots unchanged, and generate a current-version snapshot to record the new forward-compatible behavior. Alternatively, explicitly set `allowUnknownOptionalFields: false` to retain the previous behavior and avoid a new snapshot.

For example, if the snapshot directory contains `3.9.0.json`, leave that file unchanged and regenerate snapshots so a new `3.10.0.json` records `allowUnknownOptionalFields: true`:

```text
schema-compatibility-snapshots/
├── 3.9.0.json  # Retained with allowUnknownOptionalFields: false
└── 3.10.0.json # Added with allowUnknownOptionalFields: true
```

If the schema must remain strict instead, opt out before rerunning the snapshot test:

```typescript
class StrictPerson extends schemaFactory.object(
  "Person",
  {
    name: schemaFactory.string,
  },
  {
    allowUnknownOptionalFields: false,
  },
) {}
```

Snapshot failures identify schemas whose compatibility contract changed, but do not verify that application cloning, equality, serialization, or reconstruction code safely handles unknown fields.

Compatibility snapshot files are now written with a trailing newline so regenerating them does not create formatting-only diffs.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

### Fix SharedTree history length tracking during trimming ([#28522](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28522))

Reading branch history no longer causes a commit-count assertion when rebasing a branch triggers history trimming. Branch lengths are now directly computed and cached on the branch itself rather than relying on event listening, which is subject to timing issues and interleaving. Reading a branch's history length after the branch is disposed now throws an error.

## ⚠️ Deprecations

### Deprecate shared object implementation classes ([#28533](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28533))

`SharedObject` and `SharedObjectCore` from `@fluidframework/shared-object-base` are deprecated. These classes will become internal in release 3.20.0. Use existing distributed data structures instead of custom subclasses. For types that do not need implementation details, use `ISharedObject` instead:

```typescript
import type { ISharedObject } from "@fluidframework/shared-object-base/legacy";

function getSharedObjectId(sharedObject: ISharedObject): string {
  return sharedObject.id;
}
```

See [issue #26284](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/26284) for details.

### Deprecate summarizer implementation APIs ([#28599](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28599))

Direct summarizer control, detailed summarizer results, and summary collection APIs from `@fluidframework/container-runtime` are deprecated. These APIs expose implementation details and are intended to become internal. The following APIs are deprecated:

- Direct control: `ISummarizer`, `ISummarizeOptions`, `IOnDemandSummarizeOptions`, and `ISummarizeResults`.
- Enqueue support: `IEnqueueSummarizeOptions` and `EnqueueSummarizeResult`.
- Result stages: `SummarizeResultPart`, `SubmitSummaryResult`, `IBaseSummarizeResult`, `IGenerateSummaryTreeResult`, `IUploadSummaryResult`, `ISubmitSummaryOpResult`, `SubmitSummaryFailureData`, and `SummaryStage`.
- Result metadata and acknowledgements: `IRetriableFailureError`, `IGeneratedSummaryStats`, `IBroadcastSummaryResult`, `IAckSummaryResult`, and `INackSummaryResult`.
- Collection and message wrappers: `SummaryCollection`, `ISummary`, `IAckedSummary`, `ISummaryOpMessage`, `ISummaryAckMessage`, and `ISummaryNackMessage`.
- Collection watchers and events: `IClientSummaryWatcher`, `ISummaryCollectionOpEvents`, `OpActionEventName`, and `OpActionEventListener`.

For application-requested summaries, use `loadAndSummarize` from `@fluidframework/container-loader/legacy`. This is the recommended migration API for most customers:

```typescript
import { loadAndSummarize } from "@fluidframework/container-loader/legacy";

// props supplies the loader services and request.
const { version, referenceSequenceNumber } = await loadAndSummarize(props);
```

`loadAndSummarize` manages loading and disposing the summarizer container and requests an on-demand summary without requiring the application to manage summarizer implementation details. It waits for service acknowledgement and returns the acknowledged snapshot version and the reference sequence number of its summary proposal. Use `version` with `LoaderHeader.version` on drivers that support loading snapshot versions. The API rejects on failure. Enqueueing, collection watching, and detailed stage promises are implementation-level controls that are intentionally not exposed by this API.

The older `loadSummarizerContainerAndMakeSummary` API is intended for specialized integrations that do not provide service acknowledgement ops. Most customers should use `loadAndSummarize` instead. The older API's success requires submission and broadcast, and its proposal handle is not guaranteed to identify an acknowledged snapshot version.

`SummaryTreeBuilder` and `convertToSummaryTreeWithStats` from `@fluidframework/runtime-utils` are also deprecated as implementation utilities intended to become internal. There is no supported replacement for these tree-building and conversion utilities. The loader API is not a replacement for building summary trees.

This change preserves existing exports, signatures, and behavior. Internal implementations in the Fluid Framework repository can continue using these APIs. No internalization version or date is specified.

### Add oldestSupportedClient across runtime layers ([#28537](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28537))

Runtime and data store contexts now expose the required `oldestSupportedClient` property beside `minVersionForCollab`. Consumers can use `context.oldestSupportedClient` directly instead of `context.minVersionForCollab`. The runtime retains its internal fallback for older contexts that expose only `minVersionForCollab`, so mixed-version packages remain supported.

`IFluidParentContext.minVersionForCollab` is deprecated in 3.10.0 and will be removed in a future release. Use `IFluidParentContext.oldestSupportedClient` instead.

```typescript
const oldestSupportedClient = context.oldestSupportedClient;
```

The on-disk schema and telemetry property names do not change. See [the migration issue](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/27851) for more details.

### On-demand summaries can return an acknowledged snapshot version ([#28613](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28613))

`loadAndSummarize` creates a summary and waits for service acknowledgement. It returns an `AcknowledgedSummary` with required `version` and `referenceSequenceNumber` fields, and rejects on error. Use `version` with `LoaderHeader.version` to load the acknowledged snapshot. The reference sequence number comes from the matching summary proposal and identifies the document state captured by the summary.

```typescript
import { LoaderHeader } from "@fluidframework/container-definitions/legacy";
import {
  loadExistingContainer,
  loadAndSummarize,
} from "@fluidframework/container-loader/legacy";

// props supplies the loader services and request.
const { version, referenceSequenceNumber } = await loadAndSummarize(props);
const container = await loadExistingContainer({
  ...props,
  request: {
    ...props.request,
    headers: { ...props.request.headers, [LoaderHeader.version]: version },
  },
});
// Use container, then dispose it when finished.
```

`loadAndSummarize` rejects if summarization cannot recover from NACK, timeout, or premature container termination. The runtime handles summary-stage retries. The loader retries every failed attempt once with a fresh container, regardless of error retryability. A fresh load can succeed if a transient condition has resolved, but recovery is not guaranteed. Both returned values identify the successful attempt. The summarizer container is disposed before the promise settles.

`loadSummarizerContainerAndMakeSummary` returns `summaryResults.summaryInfo.handle`, which identifies the broadcast summary proposal. It is not guaranteed to identify an acknowledged snapshot that can be loaded with `LoaderHeader.version`. Use the `version` returned by `loadAndSummarize` when an acknowledged snapshot version is required.

### Use the register collection interface instead of its implementation class ([#28558](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28558))

To keep applications independent of implementation details, the package no longer exports `ConsensusRegisterCollectionClass`. As a result, applications can no longer construct or subclass that class directly.

For instance annotations, use [`IConsensusRegisterCollection`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/register-collection/iconsensusregistercollection-interface) or the [`ConsensusRegisterCollection`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/register-collection/consensusregistercollection-typealias) type alias. To create a collection, use the existing [`ConsensusRegisterCollection`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/register-collection/#consensusregistercollection-variable) creation value instead of the implementation constructor, as shown below.

```typescript
import {
  ConsensusRegisterCollection,
  type IConsensusRegisterCollection,
} from "@fluidframework/register-collection/legacy";

const registers: IConsensusRegisterCollection<string> =
  ConsensusRegisterCollection.create(runtime);
const factory = ConsensusRegisterCollection.getFactory();
```

These replacements leave collection interfaces, events, factories, handles, and persisted data formats unchanged. For the removal plan and existing deprecation, see [issue #26691](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/26691).
